chapter: Brass bands and coming to New Orleans
title: Arriving in New Orleans in 1913 and joining the Excelsior
summary: Arriving in 1913, he had trouble getting hired because he could not read or play by head, then joined the Excelsior as a regular.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, about how far back did those bands go? Were they already playing when you came to New Orleans?

Oh, yeah, yeah, yeah. They were playing. When I came here, because when I came here, I didn't get in no band for a good while. I went away for a while. I didn't know nobody. You understand what you mean?
Well, how long did it take you to get with a band? Came here in 1913.
After they found us, you understand what kind of man I was, I couldn't, the rest, I couldn't. They didn't think they'd come and knock them to do.
Well, what about, before the Big Storm, were you playing with bands?
Before the Big Storm, were you playing with bands?
Yeah, the Big Storm here. Well, yeah, yeah, yeah. You were playing with bands?
Yes. See, the Big Storm was in September of 1950.
Sure, sure. And you came here in 1913. Good man. So it wasn't too long. Well, you know. I guess it just seemed long when you were new in the city and things like that.
Well, but I'm going to tell you, you see, when I first came here, some of the guys wouldn't hire me because he would say I couldn't play home, switch home by head.

You understand? Well, of course, which I couldn't, you understand, but because of me, I always developed the region, you understand? And so, and then after that, they found out that I could do both of them, you see. So, I got in the Exelter, and they hired me on my good night, you know, on my good night. And, uh, I was a regular man, first time one day. I stayed there until they broke that.
